name: AMD EPYC 9554 (64c Genoa, 1P, 12x DDR5-5600), llama.cpp: Llama-3.3-70B Q4_K_M decode tok/s
methodology: THIRD-PARTY MEASURED (ahelpme.com EPYC 9554 bench, llama-bench, --numa distribute). EPYC 9554 64-core single socket on 12x DDR5-5600 channels (~460.8 GB/s theoretical): Llama-3.3-70B Q4_K_M 7.12 tok/s; DeepSeek-R1-70B Q4_K_M 7.11; QwQ-32B Q4_K_M 13.9. The prior '~4-6 tok/s' estimate for 70B is slightly LOW for a fully-populated Genoa - measured is ~7. CRITICAL: every channel must be populated - llama.cpp discussion #3167 measured a Genoa box with ONE 64GB DIMM at 1.5 tok/s on 34B Q4_0, jumping to 4 tok/s with a second stick.
notes: The 'big channel count' CPU play. Decode is bandwidth-bound - channels x MT/s is the spec that matters, not cores. The 2026 problem is the RAM cost: 64GB DDR5 RDIMMs went ~$873 (Q1) toward a projected ~$1,586 (Q4); a 384GB DDR5 build is $4,000-5,200+ of RAM alone - more than four used RTX 3090s. A complete Genoa box lands ~$7,000-8,000+. Legit niche: cheapest way to RUN a 400B-class model at all (~1.5-2 tok/s, overnight batch) with ik_llama.cpp fused MoE. MoE is much better: EPYC 9454P does 63.1 t/s on Qwen3-MoE-30B.
